items.notes: My own Gaia DR3 calculation matches: 10.442 arcsec x 29.516 pc = 308.2 au. Spectral types disagree: M1 (Rojas-Ayala 2012; Newton 2014), M0.64 (Terrien 2015), M2.0V (Alonso-Floriano 2015, which SIMBAD shows). M1 is the majority and fits M_G = 8.87. Teff: Terrien 2015 gives 3567 K, Rojas-Ayala 2012 3663 +/- 15 K; I took Terrien for its self-consistent Teff/R/L set. I do not recommend Mugrauer 2019 (0.572 Msun, 3901 K), because it corrects a star at 29.5 pc for A_G = 0.595. Gaia DR3 has no astrophysical_parameters for this source.

items.reason: HD 21175 (GJ 3222) is the visual binary WDS I 468. Philipot et al. 2023 (Sect. 3.2, Table 2) re-detect B with SPHERE at 2.628 arcsec, and Gaia DR3 resolves it at 2.595 arcsec with a matching parallax (56.48 vs 56.56 mas). The Systems row counts one star.
items.notes: The companion's existence and separation are high confidence; its physical parameters are low to medium. I found nothing published (SIMBAD, Mugrauer 2019, Gonzalez-Payo 2024, web search), so mass, Teff and L are all derived. Gonzalez-Payo 2024 list HD 21175 as a planet host (Table B.1) but not as a pair in Table B.4. ORB6 has an indeterminate grade-5 orbit (Izmailov 2019): P = 217.7 +/- 31.3 yr, a = 2.3285 +/- 0.1084 arcsec (41.2 au at 17.68 pc), e = 0.485 +/- 0.064, i = 41.8 deg. Kepler III on it gives a total of 1.47 Msun, consistent with 0.89 + 0.48. Because grade 5 means indeterminate, I recommend 'projected'. The writer may instead use 'semi-major axis' 41.2 au (derived), with Orbit source 'Izmailov 2019, AstL 45, 30 (ORB6 grade 5)'.

items.reason: Ross 458 (GJ 494) is a 0.43 arcsec M0.5+M7 visual binary with a solved 13.7 yr orbit (Mann et al. 2019 Table 5; Feng et al. 2022 Table 3). The sheet is missing Ross 458 B (GJ 494 B). The wide T8.5 dwarf Ross 458 C is already on the Planets tab as the planet 'Ross 458 c'.
items.notes: Which object is missing: SIMBAD's 'Ross 458 C' (= GJ 494 C = WISEP J130041.65+122114.6, T8.5p, ~102 arcsec) is the Planets tab's 'Ross 458 c' (6.00 MJup, a = 1100 au, projected, Burgasser et al. 2010). It has no Multi-stars row and should stay a planet. The missing object is B, the M7 companion at ~5 au, which SIMBAD does not list separately. After the fix the system has two stars (A and B) plus planet c. Planet c orbits the A+B pair (a 4.9 au inner binary versus a ~1100 au planet), yet its Planets row says 'Orbits the primary? = yes'; the writer may want to mark it circumbinary, like RR Cae b. Disagreements: (1) Feng 2022's a = 4.757 au with P = 13.678 yr implies Mtot = 0.575 Msun, while Mann's measured angular orbit gives 0.666 +/- 0.035 (Hipparcos parallax) or 0.634 (Gaia DR3 parallax). Feng's a is a Kepler-III value from an adopted stellar mass, not a measurement, so I recommend Mann's orbit for the separation. The mass comes from Feng because it is the only published individual mass for B; the Mann relation would give 0.098 Msun. (2) Host mass: the Systems row says 0.6, while the Mann relation gives A = 0.558 Msun, consistent with the dynamical total minus B. I have not changed it here. Feng's e = 0.245 +/- 0.001 agrees with Mann's 0.2436.

incidental_finds: GJ 3222 (HD 21175) Systems row: the distance of 59.48 ly disagrees with the Gaia DR3 parallax of 56.5570 +/- 0.0270 mas for source 4852870701505115904, which gives 57.67 ly. SIMBAD and Gonzalez-Payo 2024 Table B.1 both give 17.7 pc (57.7 ly). Source: Gaia DR3 TAP.

GJ 3222 (HD 21175): ORB6 carries a grade-5 (indeterminate) visual orbit for WDS I 468 AB (Izmailov 2019, AstL 45, 30): P 217.7 yr, a 2.3285 arcsec, e 0.485. Feng et al. 2022's 52 MJup 'GJ 3222 c' (3.9 yr, 2.39 au) is on no tab; any RV or astrometric trend in this system should be weighed against the 0.48 Msun star at ~46 au. http://www.astro.gsu.edu/wds/orb6/orb6orbits.txt

TOI-1801: Mallorquin et al. 2023 (Sect. 4.2) give the LP 375-24 separation as 101.14 arcsec, but Gaia DR3 positions give 105.05 arcsec, matching Gonzalez-Payo 2024 (105.1) and WDS 2016 (105.1). The Systems row's host mass and Teff are blank; Mallorquin 2023 Table 1 give 0.548 +/- 0.048 Msun and 3863 +/- 77 K. TOI-1801's Gaia DR3 parallax of 32.3697 mas puts it at 100.76 ly, beyond the 100 ly cut (already reported by B12). https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10244

Gonzalez-Payo et al. 2024 Table B.4 give the LP 375-23/24 discoverer code as 'LDS 626', but WDS (B/wds/wds) and SIMBAD have LDS 926. https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=J/A%2BA/689/A302

Mugrauer 2019 (MNRAS 490, 5088, Table 2) applies A_G = 0.595 mag to HD 46375 B at 29.5 pc, so its mass (0.572) and Teff (3901 K) for that star are biased high. The Gaia DR3 M_G without extinction is 8.87 (~M1V), and the Mann-relation mass is 0.52. https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=J/MNRAS/490/5088

Ross 458 c (Planets tab) is marked 'Orbits the primary? = yes', but Ross 458 is a 4.9 au A+B binary, so c at ~1100 au is circumbinary. Separately, Feng et al. 2022 Table 3's GJ 494 B a = 4.757 au does not match Mann et al. 2019's measured angular orbit (427.73 mas, i.e. 4.92-5.00 au); it implies Mtot 0.575 Msun against Mann's dynamical 0.666 +/- 0.035. https://arxiv.org/src/1811.06938v2/anc/Table5.mrt

Rejected candidates tab: the host of TOI-1760.01, 'TOI-1760', is TIC 420112587, the bound companion of TOI-1452 (Cadieux et al. 2022 Table 4). If the companion is added as 'TOI-1452 B', the Rejected row could say so. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06333
The HD 46375 and GJ 3222 Systems rows have a blank 'Planet-host class' although 'Stellar Class' is filled (G9 V and K0V). Source: this workbook.
